title: MLS Predictions: Several Teams Claw for Playoffs in Matchday 34
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Sophia Vesely4:47 PM EDTMatchday 34 will be filled with intense duels. / Peter Joneleit/Icon Sportswire/Getty Images (Lionel Messi); Maddie Meyer/Getty Images (top right); Jeff Dean/MLS/Getty Images (bottom right)It’s down to the wire. Matchday 34 of the 2026 MLS season is the second-to-last one, seeing Nov. 7’s Matchday 35 serve as the playoffs-defining Decision Day—the very last opportunity for teams to clinch a postseason berth.

Six teams from the Eastern Conference and six from West have already punched their tickets, meaning three from each side are still up for grabs. It will make for fierce battles that are anything but runaway wins.

Six teams—Red Bull New York, Toronto FC, New York City FC, LA Galaxy, Portland Timbers and Minnesota United—are staring down elimination, meaning they will bring extra scrappy energy to their respective clashes.
Here, Sports Illustrated dives into how it all may play out.

Liel Abada scored a hat trick on Wednesday. / David Jensen/Getty ImagesDate: Saturday, Oct. 31Time: 1:00 p.m. ET / 10:00 a.m. PTAn emphatic 4–0 thumping of CF Montréal midweek—highlighted by a hat trick from forward Liel Abada—should be exactly the momentum Charlotte FC needs to overcome a scrappy Orlando City squad desperate to stay above the playoff line and punch their postseason ticket.
Antoine Griezmann and Co. won’t make it easy though. They held Eastern Conference heavyweight Chicago Fire to a 2–2 draw on Wednesday at Soldier Field, despite Robert Lewandowski’s barrage of shots.
Score Prediction: Charlotte FC 3–2 Orlando City

New York City FC secured an important win midweek. / Dustin Satloff/Getty ImagesDate: Saturday, Oct. 31Time: 2:00 p.m. ET / 11:00 a.m. PTNew York City FC welcome a down-on-its-luck Montréal side to Citi Field on Saturday after securing a 2–1 win at home against Atlanta United.

NYCFC are technically still capable of making the playoffs, although all three points will certainly be needed. A loss would spell disaster. Meanwhile, the Canadians have long since said farewell to the playoffs, but are they interested in playing the spoiler?

Center back Neil Pierre has been a big reason for the Union’s resurgence. / Carly Mackler/Getty ImagesDate: Saturday, Oct. 31Time: 2:00 p.m. ET / 11:00 a.m. PTThe Philadelphia Union secured a scoreless draw on the road against Supporters’ Shield winners Nashville SC midweek. The result, which clinched a spot in the playoffs, was all the more impressive considering it came without 17-year-old prodigy and goal-contributions machine Cavan Sullivan on the pitch.
The Union stay on the road Saturday to play a rather inconsistent, yet equally unpredictable, FC Cincinnati team.
Score Prediction: FC Cincinnati 1–3 Philadelphia Union

Columbus Crew are fighting for a playoff spot. / Omar Vega/Getty ImagesDate: Saturday, Oct. 31Time: 2:00 p.m. ET / 11:00 a.m. PTThe Columbus Crew have won their last four league matches, scoring 11 goals within that span, to keep themselves just barely above the Eastern Conference playoff line. Meanwhile, D.C. United are winless in the last four league matches and firmly out of the playoff race.
Score Prediction: Columbus Crew 4–1 D.C. United

St. Louis CITY will be eyeing a return to the win column. / Rick Ulreich/Icon Sportswire/Getty ImagesDate: Saturday, Oct. 31Time: 3:00 p.m. ET / 12:00 p.m. PTSt. Louis CITY’s U.S. Open Cup victory has since been sandwiched by league losses, coming a long way from the team’s remarkable 21-game unbeaten streak earlier this season. St. Louis should finally get back into the win column, though, when they welcome San Diego FC, who will have low morale after getting thumped by the Vancouver Whitecaps 4–1 on Wednesday.
Score Prediction: St. Louis CITY 3–2 San Diego FC

FC Dallas’ Petar Musa is chasing the Golden Boot. / Seth Garber/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesDate: Saturday, Oct. 31Time: 3:00 p.m. ET / 12:00 p.m. PTSporting Kansas City are in dire form, winless in the last four matches and conceding 12 goals in that span. The league’s worst team should be no match for Western Conference powerhouse FC Dallas, who are looking to overtake the Vancouver Whitecaps for the No. 1 seed in the playoffs.
Score Prediction: Sporting Kansas City 1–3 FC Dallas

João Klauss will be tasked with pushing LA Galaxy above the playoff line. / Luiza Moraes/MLS/Getty ImagesDate: Saturday, Oct. 31Time: 5:00 p.m. ET / 2:00 p.m. PTLA Galaxy are sitting just outside the playoff line and desperately need three points to crack a Wild Card match spot. Fortunately, Austin FC shouldn’t present too much of an obstacle. The Texas side has one just one of its last seven matches—a narrow, comeback win last week over the league’s worst team, Sporting Kansas City
